title: SAUDI TV-1 (STV1)
description: Saudi TV Channel 1 (KSA 1) is a Arabic news and entertainment TV channel of Saudi Arabia.  Broadcasting throughout the Middle East, Europe and North America, KSA 1 officially began broadcasting on 7 July 1965 in black and white from Riyadh and Jeddah until 1974 when color broadcasting was introduced in Jeddah and Mecca.  Whilst the channel produces programmes focusing on cultural, political, and economic issues it is known for its showing of religious programmes and Islamic rituals.  Most notably, for being the first channel at the end of 1974 to broadcast the performance of the Hajj.  The channel is state run and is administered by the Ministry of Culture and Information.

title: AN-NAHAR
description: Profile  On august 4, 1933, the first issue of An-Nahar, a four-page newspaper, was hand-set and printed at a job printing press.  The paper, whose staff numbered five, including its founder Gebran  Tuéni, was started with a capital of 50 gold pieces raised from friends,  and a circulation of a mere 500 copies.  But soon, in less than a year, An-Nahar, bold and innovative, was able  to surpass the most deeply entrenched publications, some almost a  century old.  By 1933, Lebanon had already been laboring under the French mandate  system for 13 years. Secular, determined in its defense of Lebanon's  interests and the Arab World's wider struggle against colonial rule,  An-Nahar became the standard-bearer of the fight against social and  national injustice.  This policy earned An-Nahar readers, respect and influence. But the  price was heavy: up to the war years, both the French authorities and  the Lebanese government found it easy, and thought it rewarding, to  suspend publication of the paper.  The Second World War brought a succession of occupants to Lebanon,  different of course, but all anxious to censor the press and continue  suspending An-Nahar.  This building, in "Souk Tawileh", in the heart of the City, was home to a  dedicated team of young journalists, representatives of Beirut's  various communities, who, with Gebran Tuéni, crystallized people's  aspirations for an independent state, a better society and a  constitutional government.

title: 7 DAYS
description: Profile  7DAYS is the first urban newspaper in the UAE and the Middle East.It was originally launched as a weekly title in 2003, moving to six days a week in 2004.As a free tabloid sized colour newspaper, 7DAYS is a perfect mix of national and international news, wrapped around local information with focused, relevant features.7DAYS news stories are tightly written so that the reader can take in the key facts quickly, from breaking headlines through to sports results and celebrity gossip.  Our Readers  7DAYS is targeted at the urbanite population of Dubai, which is young, affluent and multicultural.Like other large thriving cities across the globe, Dubai’s population often work for the same multinational companies, drive the same cars, use the same mobile phones, listen to the same music and follow the same sports.Lifestyle and consumption patterns are common throughout the world, from London to Lisbon, Boston to Bangkok and Dublin to Dubai.  7DAYS chooses not to use traditional marketing strategies based on standard demographics, instead using a psychometric approach, focusing on the attitudes and values of the audience.Urbanites are aspirational and brand aware, using brands as a statement about who they are. 7DAYS is the newspaper that keeps them up to date, informed and entertained.  7DAYS Main Sections  NEWS  7DAYS brings readers the most interesting and stimulating news of the day from around the world.We offer a balanced mix of local and international stories relevant to our urban audience.Our readers are information hungry so it is up to us to keep them up to date on issues that directly affect them. We deliver these stories in a digestible, well-written format.  BUSINESS  We keep our business news accessible and incisive, while giving it the gravity it deserves. Focusing on business news that matters to the urban audience on a local, regional and international level, 7DAYS  business covers careers, technology, personal finance, marketing and business life.  METROLIFE  Smart, thought provoking and straight talking, Metrolife offers a mix of real life and topical features, guaranteed to inspire, inform, entertain and provoke a response. The style section also includes a number  of regular columns offering diverse perspectives from a team of international writers, along with informative  features on health, shopping, fashion, beauty, food and relationships.  SPORT  Sport plays a major role in the Dubai lifestyle. Not only is it a source of entertainment, but it also offers a point of unity, bringing together all of the resident nationalities.We recognise the need to deliver sports the way our readers want to read it – in an opinionated commentary style backed up by the latest statistics and results.

description: Profile  Digital studio is the Middle East’s leading magazine for the TV production, film and broadcast industries.  Today, the Middle East is one of the fastest growing broadcast markets in the world. The private sector has only just begun to invest in broadcast operations in the region, and already, it has more than 400 free-to-air channels. Along with this, initiatives like Dubai Studio City and Iraq’s Erbil Media City; the preparations to migrate to HD and the launch of new TV stations by private owners are coming to mean more business for vendors, systems integrators, rental companies and other professionals in the production and post production sectors. digital studio stands in the midst of this revolution.  With its compelling mix of industry news, on-location features, case studies, product showcases and reviews, the magazine provides a comprehensive monthly round-up of the latest developments driving the industry within the region. digital studio provides industry professionals with an insight into the latest technological developments and market trends set to impact the way they do business in the Middle East.  By ensuring the highest quality editorial content and providing the best possible news and information resource, in addition to technical analysis from experts in the field, digital studio has become a must-read for the industry’s key decision makers while it also provides the ideal platform for companies looking to promote their products and services to these trades. Digital studio has more coverage in the Middle East  North African broadcast  production sector than any other magazine in the world.  Digital studio has an equal mix of business as well as technical news. Therefore, it covers practitioners as well as the key decision makers in the industry.  Digital studio magazine is the longest serving magazine for the Middle East  North African film, broadcast  production industry. It has been reporting in the region  for more than ten years.  Digital studio is published by ITP Business, the largest trade publisher in the Middle East and North Africa. ITP Business publishes more than 30 business titles.  Digital studio distribute 9,000 copies of the magazine per month, and up to 15,000 copies on show months such as IBC, NAB, Broadcast Asia and CABSAT. title: COMMS MEA
description: Profile  Telecommunications has without doubt been the greatest boom market in the Middle East for the past five years. Infrastructure improvement contracts in all of the Middle East markets have contributed to a total spend of almost $10 billion in that time.  Saudi Arabia alone has spent almost $6 billion on public switched network and GSM network expansion projects this decade and the spending has not stopped. Telephone Expansion Project 8 (TEP8) is about to begin with the major telecommunications companies bidding for a slice of a $2 billion contract.  The key driving force for telecoms expansions this decade has been the digitisation of the networks. Today, the drive for privatisation, particularly in Africa, is creating further opportunities. Add to that the growth in overall business activity and the booming corporate PBX market and you understand why the world’s telecommunications vendors are prepared to invest so heavily in the Middle East and Africa.  CommsMEA has been serving the Middle East and African telecommunications market for almost 12 years with incisive news coverage of major developments and in-depth features about local market trends and technology issues.  The magazine’s readership is dominated by the key executives that make the decisions on major PTT projects as well as teleco managers in the major government and private organisations. Readers know that if they need to keep abreast of how to improve the service their telecommunications equipment delivers to customers and colleagues, they need to read CommsMEA. It has consistently proved that it is first to the news, and can dig underneath the story to create articles that are immediately relevant and useful to its readers.  CommsMEA is dedicated to the interests of its readership in the Arab League states and the African continent. The magazine covers every aspect of communications equipment, products, services and usage in those regions, with a particular emphasis on the provision of cost-effective solutions to problems encountered by users and service providers.

title: CHANNEL M.E
description: Profile  Introduction  An indispensable and widely respected read for the entire IT channel community, Channel Middle East is tailored to the needs of the region’s IT distributors, resellers and systems integrators, giving them the information they need each month to grow their businesses and increase profit ability.  Covering the entire IT spectrum, from high-end software channels through to commodity boxes, Channel Middle East targets the salespeople and executives that shape customer buying decisions and reseller strategies, offering them a compelling mix of original news, incisive analysis and in-depth features. With its content spanning topics such as emerging product areas, specific geographic markets, vendor strategies and reseller trends, Channel Middle East’s editorial team is dedicated to discussing the hot channel issues that matter to Middle East dealers. With IT and consumer electronics (CE) goods increasingly using similar routes to market and maintaining an extensive presence in the retail channel, the magazine’s English edition also now features the very latest CE channel developments via its dedicated Electronics Channel News section. title: WHAT'S ON
description: Profile  Introduction  CONTENT  What’s On is something of an institution in the UAE. Launched almost 30 years ago, we were the country’s first ever magazine, with our pages providing the lowdown on the region’s fledgling entertainment and leisure scene.  A lot’s happened in the UAE since then and, like the country itself, What’s On has transformed from its humble beginnings to become a leader in its field; when it comes to living life in the UAE there is no better guide.And the UAE’s oldest magazine is also the nation’s favourite, too.  Since we launched in 1979, What’s On has maintained its position as the region’s biggest-selling magazine, with a readership base that continues to rise.But don’t just take our word for it.  Our circulation figures are backed up by independent auditors BPA, who provide clear and honest results.  The simple fact is, our readers retu  every month because they know What’s On is the place to get the latest news on life in the emirates, on everything from camel racing to kite surfacing, fine dining to back street brunches – we know everything there is to know about the UAE, and we want to spread the knowledge.  In every issue  Features  The foundations on which the magazine was built our features are our pride and joy. Each month we tackle the big events, issues and interviews relating to what is happening in the area that month. Festivals, sports tournaments, exhibitions, it’s all in here and covered in detail  Recommendations and Reviews  It’s a dirty job but someone has to do it. We venture into every restaurant, every theme park and spa, and find out which are the very best in the UAE. Then, we simply tell our readers.  Travel  We’re super keen to ensure What’s On doesn’t sit on it’s Dubai and Abu Dhabi-based laurels. We venture into the region and far beyond to bring the best of the international entertainment scene.  Nightlife  The thriving nightlife of the region hasn’t gone unnoticed. No sir. What’s On is out every night painstakingly experiencing the best venues, sounds, sights, bites and drinks, after hours. Like we said, it’s a tough life.  At home  But we do rest. And when we do, we’re on the hunt for the best music, DVDs, TV and gaming the market has to offer.  Motoring  Cars, cars, cars. If there’s one thing the UAE is big on it’s motors and we test drive everything from top of the range two-seaters to people carriers the size of concorde.  Target Market  What’s On is aimed at people looking to make the most out of their time in the UAE.  Advertising Benefits  30 years strong, What’s On is the premium source of information for leisure, sports, entertainment and  lifestyle in-and-around the emirates.  The authoritative and respected editorial environment for your message  Official magazine to high profile, international events including the Dubai Rugby 7s, Dubai International  Film Festival  the Dubai Desert Classic

description: Profile  Introduction  The voice of middle east insurance  Policy is now in its fifth year and is recognised as the premier source of dedicated insurance industry information for the Middle East.  The magazine continues to provide up-to-date news and analysis on one of the fastest-growing markets in the world of insurance. Policy is tailored to the needs of insurance professionals and insurance purchasers alike, providing  answers for people on both sides of the debate. Insurex is also in its third year and now has the backing of Sheikh Hamdan Bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Deputy Ruler of Dubai and UAE Minister of Finance and Industry. Policy has not only documented some of the most critical developments in the regional insurance industry, but continues to play a part in those developments.  Policy also contains regular items such as a double-page insurance news map, a legal clinic, interviews and a page for readers’ opinions.  Editorial content  Policy, a bi-monthly publication, delivers:  Hard-edged news – reporting on the latest market trends and information  In-depth analysis – of all the major developments in the region  Regional market reports – comprehensive country updates from across the Middle East  International market features – from the leading insurance centres around the world  Rules and regulations – that affect day-to-day corporate decisions and buying policies  Profiles – of the region’s leading industry figures and organisation  Industry comment – regular contributions from acknowledged Middle East insurance experts  Global Exposure  Appearing in Policy whether through editorial or advertising coverage is a guaranteed way to get your company seen on a regional and international platform. With an extensive and varied readership, all the needs of advertisers are addressed, while Policy also has the power to place any editorial contributions at the heart of the debate.  Any company wishing to showcase its services or brand in the Middle East can rely on Policy to provide the most effective communication channel possible.

Hotelier Middle East has become my must read magazine for its comprehensive coverage of what is happening in the region and, more importantly, the reason behind it. Additionally it provides a great forum for industry discussion and provides useful information for our operation teams.  Fairmont Hotels and Resorts vice president regional  hotel sales Middle East and Africa Kent Cooper  We are an international recruitment and butler training company based in the United Kingdom with offices worldwide and a lot of our core busi-ness is based in the Middle East. Inter Continental Hotels Group  vice president development Phil Kasselis

title: MEET THE PRESS
description: Profile  STATION : AL Arabiya  Introduction  POLITICAL/SOCIAL PROGRAMS  “Meet The Press" is a new political weekly show on Al Arabiya News  Channel which focuses on Saudi Arabian politics within the Arab, regional,  international context, bearing in mind the crucial role which the Kingdom within the region. The show dives into the “hottest” topics and issues which have been doing the rounds in KSA / the Arab World, among top decision makers and leaders. It sheds light on these subjects and offers indepth analyzes from political, social and economic point of views, in tandem with guests from the media industry who also provide their inputs.  Each episode is broken down into two parts.  The first is a 20 minute interview segment which will feature a prominent figure / high profile decision maker discussing a Saudi related topic.  The second part brings together 4 journalists (2 permanent hosts and 2 guests) to a round table, aiming to enrich the discussion As the show’s host Dawood always strives to maintain a neutral standpoint.
summary: Profile  STATION : AL Arabiya  Introduction  POLITICAL/SOCIAL PROGRAMS  “Meet The Press" is a new political weekly show on Al Arabiya News

title: BOOK WORLD
description: Profile  STATION : AL Arabiya  Introduction  POLITICAL/SOCIAL PROGRAMS  Presented by: Ahmed Abdullah  This weekly show on Al Arabiya News Channel focuses on the latest books of interest to Arab audiences. Featured titles will mainly be Weste  releases, although a few prominent Arabic releases will also be covered.  Books from a broad range of genres / topics (such as political, social, religious and economics) will be reviewed, as discussions on popular authors who have impacted upon Arab audiences via their novels and bestsellers will be held. In each episode a prominent book title which has resonated exceptionally well with readers around the region / world will become the topic of discussion.  Two guests will commence a discussion, centered on the book’s subject matter, its author, central idea, resources from which it draws strength, etc…Each guest will present a different opinion. In addition, each episode will also highlight four other books with four different topics. These will be covered in a light manner, without any in-depth discussion.

description: Profile  STATION : AL Arabiya  Introduction  POLITICAL/SOCIAL PROGRAMS  Presenters: Hani Abou Ayash, Majdi Yazigi  Youmna Jelasi  Al Arabiya y presents the weather forecast in 3 different formats, covering regional weather conditions, daily temperatures, as well as forecasted temperatures for the upcoming day.  Al Arabiya’s daily Weather Forecast (7 days a week) extends a unique presentation format (10 times/day, 2 mins each), featuring live / pre-recorded video wall footage and maps of locations from in and around four different regions - the GCC, the Levant, Iraq, and North Africa (Egypt + Sudan). These reports will each focus on one of the above mentioned regions. All will benefit from the Channel’s leadership in news reporting, highlighting specific weather conditions in places where events or incidents are making headline or breaking news. Daily forecasts will air from 06:30 GMT – 13:30 GMT, following which the weather for the evening as well as the following day’s forecast will be aired.  Maps: Pre-recorded fillers will display the continents (Virtual earth) along with temperature readings from primary cities. These are aired a minimum of 10 times a day (30 second duration).  Pre-recorded fillers display the One Day Forecast as a slide showcase featuring temperatures from 30 cities (5 cities appear in each slide). These are aired a minimum of 10 times a day (30second duration)..

title: JORDANIAN TV
description: Profile  Corporate Vision:  JRTV is a Governmental Mode  Arabic Public Service platform that caters to local and Pan Arab viewers offering a transparent and diversified cultural Infotainment Television and Radio services in a civilized Islamic view. JRTV seeks to provide cost effective standard of excellence in broadcasting, while continuously developing the corporation in accordance to the public interests and priorities of Jordan.  Corporate Mission:  A high-quality, credible, independent and efficient public-service broadcasting operation which reflects, debates and celebrates the life, interests, concerns, culture of Jordan and its competitive niche market.  Corporate Values:  Teamwork: working together, regardless of specialization, towards the common objectives of JRTV. Achieving synergy, through the exchange of expertise, information and ideas that will contribute to JRTV knowledge and reflect on organizational performance.  Commitment: deeper understanding of local audience needs, and provide satisfactory TV and radio programs.  Change management: continuous improvement to develop and maintain efficient managerial decision making as well as to sustain a well trained workforce, with the aim at fulfilling the vision and goals of JRTV.  Open communication climate: communication is at the core of efficient operations, integration and coordination between employees and divisions.  Excellence: In service delivery through quality processes and workforce; and to show pride of efforts in JRTV community.  Employee empowerment: encouragement of individual creativity.  History:  Television transmission in Jordan started in black and white in April 1968 from one studio, with three hours of programming.  The following years witnessed several milestones for JTV. In 1972, it became the first station in the region to operate a second channel, Channel 2, which specialized in foreign programmes, including a news bulletin in English.  In 1974, JTV started transmission in full colors using the PAL-B system, and in 1975, transmission was expanded to cover the entire Kingdom.  Along with the English programmes on Channel 2, JTV started transmission of French news bulletins and programmes in 1978.  In 1985, Jordan Radio and Jordan Television merged to form Jordan Radio and Television Corporation.  AMRA earth station was established in 1988 and was linked to the satellites: Eutelsat, Intelsat, and Arabsat.  In 1993, the Jordan Satellite Channel was launched and in 1998, a third channel was launched, Channel 3, which was devoted to transmitting the Parliamentary sessions and local and international sports.  In January 2001, the corporation underwent major restructuring. Programmes of Channel 1 and 2 were combined in one main channel. Channel 2 specialized in sports, while Channel 3 was operated in cooperation with the private sector, on the basis of two transmission periods: the morning and afternoon “Cartoon Channel” and the evening “Jordan Movie Channel”.  Today JTV transmission covers to a large geographical area that includes the following countries: The Palestinian National Authority areas, Syria, Northe  Saudi Arabia, Israel, South Lebanon and Cyprus.  Jordan TV has four channels:  Channel One (The Main Channel)  Channel Two (The Sport Channel)  Channel Three (Jordan Movie Channel)  Jordan Satellite Channel

Her newest release “Ashiqat” is the precise translation of this blend. title: MY MALL
description: Saudi Arabia and the Gulf , have the biggest Mall concentration in the world:  According to the figures of the Ministry of Commerce in Jeddah city, the number of these centres in the city exceeds 300 commercial centres with sizes ranging between small, medium and large. All the centres work with the support of the movement of  Umra  and tourists.  Likewise, Al-Riyadh city has a similar number of centres but with smaller centres than Jeddah city at an average of 20%, and thus making Saudi Arabia the centre of the biggest number of commercial centres in the world.  This situation applies on Dubai city as well.  According to the tourist and marketing establishment of the Dubai Government, there are 57 shopping malls in the city considered to be very luxurious differently from  Mall of Arabia  which will be the biggest in the world constructed on an area of 929 thousand square meters and which is expected to be launched in 2013 as it was announced.  Due to the close ties between the three Gulf cities: Dubai, Riyadh and Jeddah, and as far as the trade activities, tourist movements and commercial centres are concerned,  My Mall  magazine has become a guide for elite readers who follow up all what these centres contain, marketing and entertainment activities.  the position of markets and retail commerce  According to a study by the Middle East council for shopping centres, the expected growth in retail commerce for 2011 will reach 16.5% even though lower from 18.5% of 2009.  This is a sign of a big forthcoming prosperity which will be witnessed in the markets of the big area, motivated by a population growth considered to be the highest in the world. For example, the population of Al-Riyadh city according to the statistics of 2010 reached approximately 6 million  citizens and residents and the same number applies to Jeddah city with a higher number of non-Saudi citizens, but with wages higher than in Al-Riyadh city.  In the total, the population of Saudi Arabia has reached 30 million, a fact that justifies this huge number of trade centres and the same justified as well the need for a specialized magazine in Arabic language.  tourism activities  The average of in-between tourist activities in the Arab Gulf region has risen.  The signs of this could be seen in the increase of the number of hosts in Dubai hotels of the citizens of the member countries of the Gulf Cooperation Council at 10% in 2009 while the number of the same hosts increased 20% during the first two months of the current year in comparison with the same period of last year.  The percentage of Gulf hosts, especially the Saudis has reached 50% in Dubai hotels, and their spending reached 40% exceeding their counterparts in other countries (Al-Itihad 21-2-2010)  On the other hand, the number of Gulf tourists to Saudi Arabia has risen at the same rate whether in Al-Umra season or summer holidays, the increase was approximately 19% last year in comparison with the year 2009. And with what is happening in some famous tourist countries such as Syria, Lebanon and even Bahrain, the expectations indicate that Gulf tourism to and from Saudi Arabia will increase more than 25%.  What indicates to this is the increase in the number of flights from the cities of the United Arab Emirates (Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Al-Shareja and Ras Al-Khaima) to the main Saudi cites (Jeddah, Al-Riyadh and Al-dammam).  The Emirate Airlines has increased its weekly flights to 129, including two flights to Jeddah by the giant Airbus commercial planes A380 with a capacity for 550 passengers.  Sami Al- Hakir, the vice-executive president of Abdul Muhsen Al-Hakir Group said that the days of Eid Al-Adha which coincided with the Dubai marketing festival registered an increase in the number of Saudi visitors to Dubai. What helped the increase was that hotel prices and services which registered a record decrease becoming acceptable and normal.  Al-Hakir also clarified that the three last months registered an improvement in the functioning and sales of the tourist units possessed by Al-Hakir in Dubai compared to the performance of the beginning of the year and since the financial crisis took place.  Meanwhile, the Saudi summer resorts in the south and Jeddah witnessed an increase in the number of Gulf visitors, notably the families coming from the United Arab Emirates, during the mid-term holiday period.  the position of the advertising market  The expectations of advertising spending indicated according to Joseph Ghassoub president of the International Association of advertisement an increase of 10% during 2010 despite the retreat of 27% of the advertising spending bulk in the United Arab Emirates during 2009, according to the  Arab Centre for Research and Consultancy studies (Park). But the report launched by the Dubai Press Club in February 2010  a view to Arab Information  expected an annual growth with the start of economic recovery of 11% this year, allowing the growth of advertising market to reach 4.4 billion Dirham (1.2 billion dollar) in 2013.  the number of free-of-charge distributed magazines (with specific sales from chosen outlets)  The overall number of free-of-charge magazines in Saudi Arabia and the Gulf is estimated at fifty quarterly, monthly and weekly publications most of which are published in English, especially in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Kuwait, while Arabic language publications specialized in commercial, marketing and entertainment activities in the Saudi and Gulf markets in general is almost none.  Thereupon,  My Mall  magazine is considered the first in this field. Despite the policy of free-of-charge distribution adopted by the magazine through elite lists, it is found in chosen selling outlets in Jeddah, Riyadh and the Easte  Region at a price of 5 Ryals.

title: AL MAJALLA MAGAZINE
description: Al Majalla is a Saudi-owned, London-based political journal published in Arabic, English and Persian.  THE MAJALLA is a current affairs magazine, published weekly in both English and Arabic.  Since it was first published in 1980 from London, THE MAJALLA has been considered one of the leading political affairs magazine of the Arab world.  The Majalla, along with Sayidaty and Al Yamamah, is among popular magazines in Saudi Arabia.  The Majalla offers the readers an overview of the main weekly news, analysis and exclusive reports with a focus on political affairs.  The magazine also provides news from USA today, Time Magazine, World Monitor and MEED.  Because of its close connection with the Arab world, The Majalla has often broken stories from sources close to militant groups like the PLO, Hamas,and Al-Qaeda.  It also publishes articles written by senior Saudi princes like Prince Turki Al Faisal.  The magazine is also well known for its political cartoons, particularly those by the late Mahmoud Kahil.  These were often critical of Israel and the United States.  The Majalla sponsored London s first Festival for Arab Caricature in 1989.

title: BOAT OWNER
description: Profile  BOAT OWNER  THE MAGAZINE FOR LUXURY BOATS AND YACHTS  The first port of call for Middle East boating.  Boat Owner Middle East is the region’s leading leisure marine publication and plays an important role in a vibrant marketplace. The magazine captures the glamour, thrill and excitement of boating with glossy production values, captivating features and lively editorial.  Just as boat owners are widely regarded as stylish, intelligent and adventurous individuals, who value their lifestyle and assets; Boat Owner magazine is no different. From dinghies to superyachts, high octane racing to soothing sail cruising, Boat Owner Middle East covers a wide spectrum, yet successfully remains focused on delivering the magazine the readership and industry deserves.  Whilst we do break news, playing a valuable part in building the most dynamic boating scene anywhere in the world, is something Boat Owner Middle East is proud of. A boat is more than a vehicle; it is a lifestyle and has the potential to take you places you had never dreamed of.  Boat Owner Middle East is the Arabian Gulf’s most enthralling boating magazine, catering for both power and sail enthusiasts. Though specifically focusing on yachts from 6 to 25 metres (20 to 82ft), dedicated sections also consider the largest and most expensive yachts on the world’s oceans and their tenders.  Boat Owner Middle East speaks with an authoritative voice, featuring original content written by experienced journalists and boating enthusiasts. Selecting only news, features and reviews that are pertinent to the local market, Boat Owner Middle East is the essential read for all yachtsmen in the Arabian Gulf.  Boat Owner Middle East offers advertisers a unique medium for targeting the mode  water enthusiast’s market – individuals with a large disposable income who place high value on their leisure time.  The magazine is sold via all major newsstands and complimentary copies are distributed at marinas, chandleries, yacht clubs and selected hotels, restaurants and bars.  Our Readers  They are a wealthy bunch, with an average income of 40,500 per month  They love to travel and 59% of them take 4 or more holidays per year  They spend an average of 42,370 AED per holiday  The majority of them own their own boat  They adore the magazine – 100% of them would recommend it to a friend  Once they have read it they pass it on and 70% of copies are read by 4 or more people.  They find the magazine informative and stylish  Quotes  “Boat Owner Middle East Magazine is an informative and easy read. I am glad to see a magazine keeping up with the times and reporting up to date issues to the growing boating market in this region.”  Joe Goddard B.E., Capt. Class V, Yachtmaster, GM Emaar Properties PJSC (Dubai Marina Yacht Club L.L.C.)  “Boat Owner Middle East is definitely one of the best regional magazines ART Marine L.L.C. is working with. We are looking forward to a long-term visible relationship through this professional, dynamic and appealing medium.”  Celine Weber, Marketing and PR Director, ART Marine L.L.C.  Reprints  Hard copy  electronic reprint service available on request, eg: 5000 copies of 5 page Fairline 64 GT boat test, February 2008.  Reprints are available in quantities of 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000. Please contact Scott Walker for more details.  The Arabian Gulf Yachting Awards 2008  Launched in 2007, the Arabian Gulf Yachting Awards are an independent set of awards designed to recognize those companies, individuals and products that have made a difference to the leisure marine industry in the GCC.  The awards were conceived as both a guide for potential boat owners who want to know who they can look to for a good product in the GCC, and to recognize companies for their outstanding contribution, work ethic and customer service. The awards celebrate the best of the best.  The Awards will take place in November 2008 at an exclusive venue in Dubai and will be attended by leading figures from the boat industry. title: CATERER
description: Profile  Caterer Middle East is a must-read among the Middle East’s executive chefs, restaurant managers, sous chefs, bartenders and sommeliers.  A dedicated food and beverage management magazine, each month the publication serves up news, culinary trends and product reviews to the Middle East’s fast-growing catering industry.  Read by more than 26,400 food service professionals, Caterer delivers cutting-edge regional and international insight, interviews, industry issues, ingredient features and new products, a well as a dedicated section for alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages.  As the Middle East strives to win a reputation as a culinary destination in its own right, a host of international celebrity chefs and brands are entering the market, while an increasing number of hotels are launching destination restaurants.  Through Caterer Middle East, food service professionals can keep up-to-date with exactly the knowledge they need to succeed in this ultra-competitive and fast-paced food service environment.  FIGURES  Read by an audience of 22,981 per month, Caterer Middle East has a monthly audited circulation of 6,566 copies.  Key geographic distribution areas include the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman and Egypt.  Readers include F B outlet owners and developers, hotel managers, F B managers, designers, human resource managers and recruitment agencies.  Results from the ITP Business Readership Survey July 2008 show more than 90% of readers consider the editorial content to be good or excellent, with more than 37% of subscribers having their copy read by five people or more.  The survey showed 81% consider Caterer Middle East to be superior to other publications within the sector in the region.  Caterer Middle East’s broad appeal translates into sales for advertisers in the magazine — 98% of readers have used the magazine to make purchasing decisions for their outlet.  TESTIMONIALS  “Caterer Middle East is the essential reference magazine for restaurant professionals, profiling the very best in products and services available and the latest trends setting standards across the region.”  Stuart Nielsen, director of F B, Inter Continental Hotels Group Dubai Festival City  “Caterer is a well put together and informative magazine, relevant to the industry here in the Middle East. I look forward to each issue rather impatiently — 30 days is too long to wait for the next edition!  This publication impressed me so much that I even decided to become a part of it by contributing a monthly chef’s column.”  Marcus Gregs, Master CGC, ECG, CRCR, executive chef, Mövenpick Hotel Bur Dubai  “During my time in the Middle East, Caterer magazine has been my link to the trade on a wider scale. It’s not an easy job to representsuch a diverse industry, but each month Caterer manages to highlight and air the topical issues that affect all of us. Not only that, the people behind Caterer actually get out there and listen to people within the industry.  Whether reporting trade-organised events or just stopping by for an informal chat, the Caterer crew represents a genuine, human touch unique within the industry, which is much needed and appreciated.”  Angus McGregor, bars manager, CCM

title: EMIRATES BRIDE
description: Profile  Emirates Bride is the faithful companion that brides-to-be rely on.  The Emirates Bride reader knows that her wedding is a vehicle to express her individuality and personal style and she knows that she’ll find inspiration on each page.  Covering everything from gowns to favours, to-do lists to honeymoons and everything in between, Emirates Bride ensures that every bride has the wedding she’s always dreamed of.  In every issue  Fashion  Today’s bride has an endless choice of flattering, show-stopping options at her disposal and our fashion team scour the world’s leading fashion houses to bring you the most up-to-the-minute choices in bridal couture each issue.  Beauty  The industry’s leading make-up artists and skincare experts spell out the must-know tricks and techniques to ensure that your wedding day glow doesn’t fade from altar to dance floor.  With inside knowledge on seasonal colours and looks, you can be assured you’ll be at your most beautiful on the day it counts most.  Real Life Weddings  Each month, we feature the real-life experiences of brides who’ve already done the walk down the aisle. Included in their romantic tales is advice on the what, where, when and how of their big day.  Sometimes, the tips of brides who’ve been there before you is all the assurance you need that you’re on the right track.  Travel  Everyone has an opinion on the most idyllic honeymoon location. So we bring you somewhere different each issue – to make sure your choice is the most best, most personal honeymoon ever.  Wedding Directory  With everything from wedding chapels to DJs, photographers to ministers, you’ll find what  you’re looking for in our wedding directory.  Constantly updated to include the newest of information, it’s the tear-out guide you’ll be glad to have on hand.  Target market  Those interested in planning a wedding covering all the details from planning the big day to fashion  accessories to health  beauty.  Advertising benefits  Brides-to-be are engaged... with Emirates Bride. They use the magazine as a trusted friend and consume this magazine with heightened interest. This includes the advertising which is considered valuable content  The most comprehensive wedding guide in the UAE.  Exposure alongside the topical editorial provides the perfect advertising environment to those planning their perfect wedding.

title: COMMERCIAL INTERIOR DESIGN
description: Profile  ITP Business is the largest publisher of trade magazines for the construction industry in the Middle East. As the publisher for one of the region’s fastest growing sectors, ITP Business’s publications cover the full spectrum of the construction sector, from the design, to the build, to the fit out and finally the management of finished residential and commercial buildings.  Currently, the ITP Business construction portfolio includes Construction Week, MEP Middle East, Commercial Interior Design, Facilities Management Middle East, and now Middle East Architect. ITP Business also delivers a number of associated award ceremonies, events, and trade show publications.  Commercial Interior Design is the leading source of ideas, inspiration and product information for industry professionals across the Middle East.  Read by senior decision makers and influences from across the region Commercial Interior Design is delivered to 13,873 readers each month and has a pass on readership of over 55,000.  Commercial Interior Design covers all aspects of commercial interiors, from residential to industrial, offices to retail outlets, hotels to health spas and everything in between. Kitchens, bathrooms, flooring, office furniture, lighting, fixtures and fittings all have a home in Commercial Interior Design, along with everything industry professionals need to create attractive and prof table commercial interiors.  Commercial Interior Design has become an essential monthly read for interior design professionals across the GCC.  Containing the latest local and international news, product launches and project focuses, contract wins and tender invites, Commercial Interior Design offers readers the opportunity to get to grips with key industry trends and opportunities.  Whether you are a designer looking for inspiration from abroad, a specifier looking for the latest products, or an architect seeking ideas then Commercial Interior Design is for you.  Commercial Interior Design is part of the Construction Week stable of titles published by ITP Business, the largest business, technology and construction trade publisher in the Middle East.  Commercial Interior Design is delivered to 10,000 readers each month. With an average pass on readership of four people,  Commercial Interior Design is read by over 34,000 chief decision makers each month*  Chief executive officers, managing directors, general managers, directors, designers, specifiers and consultants from across the Middle East read Commercial Interior Design on a monthly basis. Commercial Interior Design’s readers work not only in interior design companies, architect firms and for specifiers, developers and contractors, but also in the property sector, for building owners and in the region’s governments. title: EN VOGUE
description: Profile  En Vogue –the Dubai Fashion Magazine, published by Mediamost is the magazine for the fashion connoisseurs coming from Dubai with regional distribution throughout the lower GCC countries..  The innate aim of the magazine is to promote and enhance Dubai’s international reputation as one of the leading fashion capitals of the world. The magazine will contribute to making the "Dubai Fashion" a stand-lone brand by itself.  Our international affiliates provides the magazine with the latest of runways worldwide, whereas our correspondents in Paris and Milan provide exclusive interviews with top designers.  Our local editorial team covers the latest and the hot of the shelves of prestigious Dubai boutiques. Over the past year, the magazine has positioned itself in the UAE market as a major source for trend setters in fashion and luxury items.  En Vogue has established a loyal readership base who are only satisfied by the best in lifestyle.  Credibility  En Vogue is published with close collaboration between Mediamost and the Dubai Shopping Festival committee and the Department of Tourism and Commerce Marketing.  Publishing Dates  The magazine is published Bi monthly, 6 issues a year as per the following dates:  Feb/March  April/May  June/July  August/Sep  Oct/Nov  Dec/Jan

title: GO MAGAZINE
description: Profile  Go Magazine is the definitive guide to what’s going on in Jordan. It offers information on how to get the most out of what the Kingdom has to offer. Whether it’s hiking the Mujib Reserve, go karting at the Jordan Speed Center, or enjoying a meal with friends at any one of Amman’s great restaurants, Go Magazine will inform you about it, while telling you what you’ll need to participate, as well as how to maximize your experience.  Why is Go Magazine Different?  Though we’re not attempting to reinvent the publishing industry, we are offering up a magazine that fills a gap in the market and fulfills a purpose. Which is to motivate, inspire, inform, and empower the people of Jordan to simply get up and Go!  Our approach is one grounded in experiencing first-hand what we feature in the magazine. We live what we cover as our entire team of contributors — whether they’re writers, photographers, or designers — have been hand-picked to provide our readers with the best insider information to arm them with a plethora of activities to do, places to visit, and new things to experience.

title: MBC MAX
description: MBC Max is a free-to-air movie channel that broadcasts non-stop Hollywood films (and sometimes films from other countries) 24/7 and it is an alternative to its sister channel MBC 2.  The aim of MBC Max is to broadcast more choices of films, including more MBC premieres and first-time-on-TVs, for MBC s audience in the Middle East and North Africa. However, the films features on MBC Max seem milder in content than the films featured on MBC 2, although the pre-launch promotion hinted that MBC Max was created for a wider range of film audiences.  MBC Max also features MBC 3 prints of animated and family films, always broadcasting in the middle of the afternoon U.A.E. time, as these films feature the same MBC 3-based, higher-level censorship.  Despite MBC Max s reputation for broadcasting mild films, it does however broadcast certain R-rated films, such as dramas and comedies.  Additionally, MBC Max broadcasts classical films more often than MBC 2, since the majority of Hollywood films from the 1960s and before are considered mild by today s standards.
summary: MBC Max  is a free-to-air movie channel that broadcasts non-stop Hollywood films (and sometimes films from other countries) 24/7 and it is an alternative to its sister channel MBC2.  The aim of MBC Max is to broadcast more choices of films, including more MBC premieres and first-time-on-TVs, for MBC s audience in the Middle East and North Africa.

title: MTV LEBANON
description: MTV was established in 1991 as a TV channel that sought to cater to the complexity and richness of its Lebanese viewers  identity by creating a balanced mix of local, Arab, and weste  media content, with a special emphasis on producing local programming that is tailored to its audience and reflects their aspirations and values.  In addition to its unique approach to programming, MTV also led the way in terms of its adoption of self-regulation and a clear code of ethics, in a country where the media sector is completely unregulated, thus becoming the first station to abide by international best practices while legally acquiring foreign formats and rights-to-air.  Embarking on the Political Scene  In March 1995, MTV embarked on the political scene, launching its local news broadcasts along with a number of distinct political and socio-economic shows.  MTV displayed a fervent commitment to acting as the fourth power, disclosing the untold about abuses of power and corruption, and speaking the mind of a suffocated public opinion, being consistently and unswervingly objective and responsible, and defending the public interest.  Broadcasting Revolution  In 2002, the Government engaged in an unlawful process, illegally and retroactively to forcibly close the MTV and On April 7, 2009 the voice of the  silent majority  returned to screens across Lebanon and the world.  Since then MTV has undertaking a major revolution: New look, new programs but with the same professional outlook on the future.... and will always be the voice of freedom ...  Vision  MTV s vision is to be the leading independent media station in Lebanon and the Arab world, serving as the catalyst and vehicle for inclusion and regional well-being, and endorsing reform and advancement from within societies.  MTV strives to become the indisputable symbol for the values of thought independence, social responsibility, freedom of expression and continuous betterment.  Mission  MTV s mission is to enhance the media s role in Lebanon and the Arab world, to participate in the advancement of independent thought, and to serve the interests and the well-being of society while assuring its commitment to shareholders.  MTV strives to be the region s media role model in terms of transparency and social responsibility, delivering on its pledged values by providing its viewers with content that informs, entertains, develops minds and ripens individuals, free of any bias.
summary: On April 7, 2009 the voice of the  silent majority  returned to screens across Lebanon and the world. title: CNBC BUSINESS
description: Profile  CNBC Business is a monthly business magazine that covers – and discovers – the most interesting entrepreneurs hatching the most innovative business models within the most dynamic sectors. title: HAREEM EL SULTAN
description: Profile  Starting February 10, 2012 at 20:00 KSA  Sultan Suleiman is overjoyed at becoming the ruler of the Ottomans, at the young age of 26. He looks upon his reign as an opportunity to draw greater power for the Ottomans then even Alexander did. He sets out to become the young Sultan warrior, after receiving news of his coronation in the year 1520, at the time not realizing that he would go on to rule more territories then even he could have ever imagined.  Leaving behind his wife (mahedfran), his young son (mustaffa) and his palace (Manisa), he is accompanied by his close friend Ibrahim, as they journey to reach the Topkapi Palace situated in the capital of Astana. Meanwhile, an Ottoman ship sails out to sea to collect women, who will be gifted to his palace. Alexandra La Rosa – the daughter of an orthodox Ukrainian priest is amongst them. She will stay on to become his wife and give birth to their heir - A princess who will grow up to rule alongside Suleiman, as he struggles to hold on to his position, amidst growing unrest and conspiracies, which will ultimately cost his Minister Ibrahim the blood of his own family.  Tracing the extraordinary journey of Sultan Suleiman, with all its hidden revelations and behind the scene looks at his life; this series is the biggest production of its kind in Turkish drama history.

Sultan Suleiman is overjoyed at becoming the ruler of the Ottomans, at the young age of 26. He looks upon his reign as an opportunity to draw greater power for the Ottomans then even Alexander did. title: ABU KHALEEL AL QABBANI
description: Profile  Station : OSN  Starring: Bassel Khayat  Abu Khalil Al-Qabbani is a pioneer of the mode  Arab musical theatre and one of its principal founders.  His early beginnings were in Damascus where he founded his own theatre to perform musicals. His plays were deemed extremely pro-modernization by the city's conservatives  caused a wave of protest.  The dispute ended with a decree by the Ottoman government to close his theatre and prevent theatrical performances in Syria. Stirred by his passion for art  prowess as a composer  dramatist, Al-Qabbani moved to Egypt with his troupe where the cultural and political atmosphere was more conducive to theatre.  Throughout his 17-year stay in Egypt, Al-Qabbani's performances gained huge success via which he witnessed the ultimate manifestation of his vision of a liberal Arab theatre. However, to the pro-British administration in Egypt, Al-Qabbani's anti-colonialism plays threatened Britain's existence in Egypt. The public was roused against him and his theatre was burned down, leaving him no choice but retu  home.  Unfortunately, the art that blessed Al-Qabbani with the highest ranks among his peers was the same that brought about his decline. Al-Qabbani's loss during his life might have been too vast but entailed no regrets as the legacy he left made him memorable throughout history.

title: AL HUSROM AL SHAMI PART
description: Profile  Station : OSN  Starring: Abbass Nouri, Carisse Bachar  A century has elapsed, yet Damascus witnessed neither social nor political changes, except for a few names of authority figures. In the process of “resurrecting” the Ottoman Empire that was accompanied by rebellious movements, the Damascenes were involuntarily strained among the conflicting parties because Damascus had a significant geographical advantage.  The struggle moved to Damascus when one of the influential Turkish rebels headed there and appointed himself as the capital’s sultan. The strain had a social impact on people when a married woman eloped with the son of the rebel provoking another conflict among three powerful figures who were directly affected by this scandalous event.  Typically, innocent helpless people had to pay the price and were forcibly driven to fight a war that wasn’t theirs in any way. In the absence of discipline and order, some power-seeking individuals took advantage and imposed their will on common people only to add to the prevailing injustice and suffering

title: AWLAAD AL QAIMARIYYA PART 2
description: Profile  Station : OSN  Abdallah broke the family’s tradition when he chose to work for a governmental entity and serve the public, instead of running the family’s textile warehouse with his three brothers. His professional integrity had him noticed by his superiors who promoted him to senior inspector.  The newly-acquired position put so much pressure on Abdallah as he exposed the corruption of officials and individuals. To Abdallah’s distress, his eldest brother was directly connected to such allegations and disclosure of this finding meant his brother’s imprisonment.  To hinder Abdallah’s efforts, a conspiracy is laid out behind the curtains upon which he gets killed and the murder is attributed to embezzlement. His wife Qamar too has her share of the plot and is accused of infidelity.  Qamar is left with no choice but run away with her son Shareef. She takes refuge in Turkey away from her people and two brothers. After twenty years Qamar and Shareef retu  to their old neighbourhood of (Al-Qaimariyya) but in disguise, in an attempt to know who was behind Abadallah’s murder and the scandalous rumour that ruined their lives.

description: Profile  Station : Melody Drama  Starring :  Jamal Suleiman Oriya Fargali  Written by:  Midhat Al Adel  Directed by:  Islam Kheiri  In 1977, Egypt suffers from civil unrest, as two families begin a deadly feud. Aarfan’s brother Aafak (a protester) is arrested and released after an exhausting effort. But the family’s joy is short lived, as Aafak is shot dead by the Manweeshi family.  Aarfan is pushed by his family to take revenge, but he refuses. This is when another family member kills one of the Manweeshis, and frames Aarfan, who now becomes a fugitive. Next up, Aarfan’s wife is brutally murdered, an event which forces him to run to the wilderness, fearing for his young son’s life. He adopts a Robin Hood type existence, until his son falls critically ill. In dire need of medical help for his son, Aarfan thinks about surrendering. With three wives now in tow, he decides to marry a fourth, who creates many difficulties between Fawaz and all his wives, leading to a series of events which will transform his outlook on women.

title: SIRR ALANY
description: Profile  Station : Melody Drama  Starring :  Ziyad Naser and Ghada Adil  Written by:  Mhamad Nayir  Directed by:  Ghada Saleem  Despite coming from a prominent family, Ameena runs away to London to break free of her controlling father. In the UK, she meets an Egyptian businessman named Saleh Ramzi and a relationship begins. But she soon discovers that Saleh is involved in a fraudulent money market scheme, and together with some other influential people runs illegal arms through the Arab world. As the relationship turns sour, she runs away from him and writes a book detailing the inner workings of his illicit operation.  Saleh decides to hunt her down and fights back by gaining control of the distribution rights to her book, although Ameena manages an independent print run of a thousand copies. With her personal turmoil growing by the day, Ameena attempts suicide and is saved by a doctor, who she will find a new life with.  In the backdrop, a former victim of Saleh’s, whose family had lost everything, accidently discovers Ameena’s book. Eager to take revenge, he is inspired by the plan which the book outlines on how Saleh’s gang should be brought to justice.
